messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Metering anomaly detected for prod (us-east-1). Token-count drift >7% vs baseline over 30m. Trigger: metering-telemetry. Incident ID: MTR-20260317-42. Pager sent to #incidents and oncall.
oncall_metering: grabbing this. I'm oncall for metering. @sarah @mike please ping if you see anything obvious.
sarah: looking at emitter logs now — seeing a flurry of 503s from proxy around 12:42Z, followed by retries. Pulling raw event samples.
mike: running a quick aggregate against the raw events: `SELECT sum(token_count) AS tokens FROM usage_events WHERE timestamp >= now() - interval '1 hour' AND region = 'us-east-1';` — result shows ~9% higher than rolling baseline. Also windowing looks delayed for a 2-3 minute slice.
oncall_metering: could be duplicate emission or late arrivals causing overcount. Can someone check consumer lag for kafka partition range 10-14? `kafka-consumer-groups --describe` shows lag ~0 for the metering consumer.
jordan (billing-eng): any customer-facing overage flags firing? Querying billing alert service: 12 customers received transient overage flags; one enterprise acct (3rdparty-inc) hit threshold and got an automated flag.
oncall_metering: okay — that's actionable. We should avoid billing noise. Try validating dedupe key presence (request_id) on affected events.
sarah: found a 2-minute window (12:42:00Z - 12:44:00Z) with ~5k events missing request_id — matches emitter restart timeline. Looks like emitter crashed and retried without preserving request_id.
mike: plan: run compaction/dedupe for that specific time slice. Dry-run first: `python infra/tools/dedupe.py --start 2026-03-17T12:40Z --end 2026-03-17T12:50Z --dry-run` and compare token totals.
oncall_metering: do the dry-run and post the delta. If dedupe reduces tokens close to observed drift, run full compaction and hold off billing triggers.
mike: dry-run finished — estimated reduction ~8.7% tokens in window, aligns with telemetry. Proceeding to run dedupe job now (non-dry).
incident-bot: Incident MTR-20260317-42 update: dedupe job started by mike. Logs: https://logs.re/redwood/MTR-20260317-42
jordan (billing-eng): I'm pausing automated overage emails and suppressing alerts for the affected accounts to avoid false escalation. Notifying CS for enterprise 3rdparty-inc.
natalie (cs): messaging 3rdparty-inc: "We've detected a transient metering anomaly that may have caused a spike in usage flags. We're remediating and will follow up — no invoices will be generated while we reconcile."
mike: dedupe job completed. Post-compaction token reduction 9.1% for the affected slice. Re-running billing triggers and clearing suppressed flags.
oncall_metering: reconciling ledger and pushing corrected counts through billing pipeline. Monitoring for 30m. If stable, we'll close the incident.
jordan (billing-eng): reconciliation run complete — counts back to baseline, suppressed overage flags cleared. No charges were generated. Action items: (1) emitter must never emit null request_id; (2) add a quick metric alert for spikes in null_request_id_rate; (3) add a pipeline guard to avoid auto-emailing when dedupe_compaction_in_progress. Assigning to alex.
alex: taking ownership of the emitter fixes and the alert. I'll open PRs: harden request_id preservation, add null_request_id alert, and change billing pipeline to respect a dedupe-in-progress flag.
oncall_metering: incident closed: MTR-20260317-42 — root cause: emitter crash + client retry pattern produced duplicate events without dedupe key. Mitigation: targeted compaction/dedupe, suppression of overage emails, and billing reconciliation. Postmortem scheduled for tomorrow. :white_check_mark:
